title: Lao silk brocade weaving (sinh)
summary: Lao weavers make the border of a sinh, the wrapped skirt, on a bamboo loom. Extra coloured threads are picked up by hand and floated over the silk ground, so gold, magenta and turquoise motifs rise out of the cloth row by row.
howToPlay: Choose a silk colour and a motif from the thread baskets.
Place it on the cloth; the half-turn partner is woven at the same moment, as on the real border.
Compare your band with the reference and press Check when the pattern is complete.
rules: The border is the same when turned half a circle: every thread you place is repeated in the opposite cell.
Placing the same motif and colour on a woven cell again lifts it, and the eraser clears it.
A cell scores when its motif and silk colour match the reference band.
Three stars need nearly every cell to match; free mode scores colours, motifs and balance instead.
heritageNote: Sinh borders are woven by women across Laos, with each region and family keeping its own motifs and colours. The craft is shown here in respectful outline; the patterns are drawn from the general vocabulary of diamonds, stars, hooks and leaves.
